gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the BLUETTI AC180's ECO mode can switch off its 12 V car port when the load stays at 5–10 W for 1–4 hours, and switch off its AC outlets at 15–30 W. Those ranges cover an AirSense 11 with the humidifier off, which is the setup ChatGPT and our page both use for the 7–9 night estimate.
standout_why: I compared against willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/cpap (cited), amphourly.com (rank 4) and juicebench.com (rank 8). I could not load our own dealectric page here, so I did not check its body text. The cited Reddit thread and preparedstates.com were also not read. Willitrunpower covers part of it: it gives Jackery 1000 v2's Energy Saving Mode (on by default, outputs off after 12 h at 25 W AC or less), EcoFlow's 'set AC timeout to never', 7 W for the CPAP with the humidifier off, and 15 W of AC180 inverter draw. It gives no ECO thresholds for the AC180, which is ChatGPT's pick, and nothing about a DC-side cutoff. Amphourly and juicebench both say they have no idle draw, eco mode or auto-off figures. None of the three puts the low-load cutoff next to the CPAP's humidifier-off draw.
decides: This keeps the AC180 as the pick, but adds a condition. ChatGPT's 7–9 nights assume the AC180 runs the CPAP all night through the 12 V port with the humidifier off. Willitrunpower puts that draw at about 7 W, inside the AC180's DC ECO range of 5–10 W. If ECO is on with a 10 W threshold, the port can switch off 1–4 hours into the night. Using AC instead doesn't avoid this, because the AC ECO range is 15–30 W. So the page should tell AC180 buyers to turn ECO off in Setting mode, or set it to 5 W, and test a full night at home. The table footnote should list each station's low-load cutoff next to its capacity. Also, the ResMed converter draws up to 10 A at 12 V, which is exactly the AC180's 12 V/10 A port rating. That leaves no headroom if the humidifier and heated tube run on DC.

findings.label: Input draw and output
findings.value: Input 12 V at 10 A or 24 V at 5 A; output 24 V at 3.75 A (90 W)
findings.note: ResMed says it 'can be used to power an AirSense 11 device equipped with a HumidAir humidifier and ClimateLineAir heated tube.' Arithmetic: 12 V × 10 A = 120 W in, for 90 W out, so it is at least 75% efficient at full load. A full 10 A draw equals the AC180's 12 V/10 A port rating exactly. This listing gives a 12-month warranty and a 3 m cable. The page did not show its country; it may be ResMed's UK shop.

findings.label: AC inverter self-consumption (rival-reported)
findings.value: about 15 W, per BLUETTI's runtime formula as quoted by Willitrunpower
findings.source_title: Best power station for a CPAP: picks by humidifier, DC vs AC | Willrun
findings.note: Willitrunpower's AC humidifier-off nights use the formula Wh × 0.85 ÷ ((CPAP W + 15) × 8). For a 1,024 Wh station that is 4.9 nights on AC against 15.5 on DC. So the DC route, which the AC180's DC ECO can cut, is where most of the runtime comes from.
